source: NCERT Class IX, Democratic Politics I, Polity Ch. 3.

sections.heading: 1. Why Elections
points: **Elections** let people **choose their representatives** at regular intervals and hold them accountable.
Elections make **representative democracy** possible in large countries.
In a democratic election: everyone can choose (**universal adult franchise**), there is a **real choice**, elections are held **regularly**, and the process is **free and fair**.

sections.heading: 2. India's Electoral System
points: The country is divided into **constituencies**; voters in each elect **one representative** (**First-Past-The-Post**, FPTP — the candidate with the most votes wins).
**Reserved constituencies** for **SCs and STs** ensure their representation.
**Lok Sabha** has 543 elected seats; **Assembly** elections choose MLAs.
**Universal adult franchise** — every citizen **18+** can vote.

sections.heading: 3. The Election Process
points: Steps: **notification → nomination of candidates → election campaign → polling → counting → results**.
**Electoral rolls (voter lists)** are prepared; a **Voter ID / EPIC** is issued.
**Voting** is by secret ballot using **Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs)** with **VVPAT**.
The **Model Code of Conduct** governs campaigning.

sections.heading: 4. The Election Commission
points: The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** is an **independent** constitutional body that **conducts and controls** all elections.
It is headed by the **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC)**.
Its independence and powers make Indian elections **largely free and fair**, though challenges (money, muscle power) remain.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Democratic election: universal franchise + real choice + regular + free and fair.
System = First-Past-The-Post (FPTP), one representative per constituency; reserved seats for SC/ST.
Voting age = 18; EVMs + VVPAT; secret ballot; Model Code of Conduct.
Election Commission of India = independent body, headed by CEC.
Lok Sabha = 543 elected seats.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: India uses the **First-Past-The-Post (FPTP)** system — the candidate with the **most votes** wins the seat.
**Reserved constituencies** exist for **SCs and STs**.
The **Election Commission** is an **independent constitutional** body (headed by the CEC).
Voting age is **18** (universal adult franchise).
